Logix alone develops the Apple II and S-100 expansion cards; these demonstrate Adam’s ecosystem intentions and are not DRI obligations. Apple cards expose FlexiBUS and video to native Apple software. CP/M-6502 is deferred, with no product, schedule or cost commitment. Published interfaces and affordable developer access permit competing software, cards, peripherals and monitors. AION retains Abacus, C tools, Business Tools, AIONix and the existing Pulse offering; DRI licenses CP/M independently. BPI operates independently under its own brand from the cooperation period. Any further ownership separation around 1985 remains a future transaction, not the beginning of operational independence or a completed buyout.

Five partners begin preparation in January 1981 for a January 1982 coordinated launch. They retain their brands and may build mainboards, contract manufacture or buy Logix boards; buy custom chips from AION or qualified SGS; source qualified RAM freely; design local chassis/keyboards; and buy conforming monitors from Logix or others. Anything outside an initial range may be supplied by Logix or third parties, with clear warranty and integration ownership. No partner must manufacture a complete catalogue.

AION Software delivers and maintains German, French and Spanish CP/M/TUI, AIONix, Business Tools, Abacus and programming environments, coordinating underlying OS rights and release approval with independent DRI. Use common APIs, document formats and shared cores with local resources. Validate keyboards, accents, fonts, printing, sorting, numbers, currency and dates. Clone manufacturers separately license other publishers including WordStar, dBASE and BPI; statutory accounting/payroll adaptation requires separate local qualification. UK English editions and support serve Aion Tech. Localisation is not a national software fork.

These agreements, preparations and January 1982 launches are accepted narrative additions. Existing ecosystem projections already include North Star and Vector; replace their unsigned-prospect assumptions in the next numerical reassessment, never add their sales twice. Germany, France, Spain and Aion Tech require country forecasts. No automatic sales multiplier is awarded for the launch. Transfer funding, localisation, pilot lots, marketing, Academy staffing, working capital and chip capacity must be costed before a revised investment/ROI claim; The 1981–1983 numerical planning reassessment is recorded in sales_reassessment_inputs.json, sales_forecast.json and roi_1974_1980.json; provisional transfer prices and capacity allowances are not signed contract terms. Aion Tech ownership and consolidation remain open.

SGS receives a non-exclusive independent manufacture-and-sale licence for ERAv1 and all agreed custom controllers, including MMU, system, bus, storage, network and video controllers. Each part and speed grade qualifies separately. ERAv1 stays on 3 µm; no shrink is implied. Preserve existing SMC rights. AION provides launch supply for parts not yet qualified at SGS, so January clone delivery does not depend on simultaneous qualification of the entire portfolio.

Adam commits to supplying the staffing, equipment, licences and integration resources required by the agreed delivery plan. No arbitrary dollar ceiling or fabricated cost estimate; procurement and staffing are reviewed against the November objective. Non-exclusive funded development. Autodesk retains its software ownership and cross-platform business; clear the underlying Interact contribution/porting rights with the founders, including Mike Riddle. Logix supplies distribution and joint marketing, without a source buyout or forced platform exclusivity. Professional 17-inch/800x600 hardware becomes available around June, not January. See team_development_program.json for deployment and acceptance requirements. Sponsorship is incremental project work, not counted as retail Team Edition sales. The 1981–1983 reassessment includes an explicit planning provision for sponsorship and conditional CAD demand; see sales_reassessment_inputs.json. This is not a contractual funding ceiling, supplier quotation or confirmed shipment count.

Athena base: 2 × 128 KiB 2 µm 4164 modules and 5 MB HDD. Server: 4 × 256 KiB modules and 20 MB HDD. Both: ERA², 64 KiB graphics, one 5.25-inch DS/DD FDD, NIC, EEPROM BIOS and 256 KiB directly executable AIONix2 system ROM. No external application cartridge slots are added. AIONix2 has an accepted phased design baseline; implementation and measured fit remain qualification gates. All ERA² architectural numbers are engineering targets, with 16 MHz a stretch bin. AION Labs alone manufactures ERA² initially; SGS-ATES excluded for at least 12–18 months after initial commercial availability. Development dates are provisional; cost and financial forecasts remain unchanged.

public date: 1979-06-04
profiles: Optional versioned extensions separate from the CP/M core; neither FlexiBUS nor Logix video is mandatory for all CP/M applications.
continuity: Fund CP/M maintenance alongside the next-generation programme; detailed duration and budget remain open.
qualification: Named host/ISA/TPA/application editions and file interchange; no universal Aurelia binary or disk compatibility promise.

eligibility: Any manufacturer or independent integrator may implement the published environment without a bespoke partnership or mandatory certification.
binary: Existing Z80 binaries require compatible instruction execution and the specified OS/runtime and memory behaviour; CP/M alone is insufficient. Other processors need an appropriate port or execution solution.
hardware: Native video, keyboards, disks and printers may be exposed through adapters. FlexiBUS and Logix video hardware are separate optional profiles. Full hardware clones may implement those published interfaces under their applicable terms.
applications: Named supported platforms are tested configurations, not an exclusive permission list. Independently implemented environments may run properly licensed applications; certification identifies precisely what AION tested.
scope: Released 8-bit Aurelia interfaces only. No future processor names, word size, ISA, binaries or architectural details before NCC 1980.
licensing: Specification and self-test requirements are freely accessible. Kit fee covers media, manuals and updates supplied with the kit. Reference runtime adapters may be modified and redistributed without per-machine royalty under standard terms. No automatic licence to redistribute CP/M, application binaries, firmware or trademarks; obtain each required licence separately. Proprietary application source is not included.
delivery: Printed manuals/source listings and disks; host/media conversion quoted separately.
certification: Optional, configuration- and version-specific. Manufacturer-declared compatibility is distinct from AION-tested application compatibility. FlexiBUS electrical/protocol and Logix display tests are separate claims.
